questions.q: How does a B-tree index speed up a query?
questions.a: It keeps keys in sorted order in a balanced tree, so the database finds a value or a range in logarithmic steps instead of reading every row.
An index that contains every column a query needs, so the database can answer from the index without reading the table rows.

questions.q: Why might a query ignore an index?
questions.a: The predicate cannot use it (a function on the column, a leading wildcard), the table is small enough that a scan is cheaper, the planner expects most rows to match, or statistics are stale.

questions.q: What is the cost of too many indexes?
questions.a: Every write maintains each index, so inserts and updates slow down, and indexes take memory and disk. Index for the queries you actually run.
